author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Helena Foulkes defeated Rhode Island Gov. Dan McKee in Wednesday’s Democratic primary, ending his campaign for a second full term and producing one of the night’s most significant incumbent losses.

The former CVS and Hudson’s Bay executive turned a 2022 primary defeat into a victory in the rematch. McKee became the first governor in any state to lose a party primary since 2018 and the first sitting Rhode Island governor to be beaten in a primary in more than 30 years.

The Washington Bridge dominated the campaign. The older westbound span was abruptly closed in 2023 after structural problems were found, and delays and costs associated with its replacement fueled commuter frustration. Foulkes argued that the project reflected broader management failures, while McKee defended the closure as necessary for public safety.

McKee conceded Wednesday night and said his administration would support a smooth transition. Foulkes now advances to the November 3 general election, where she will face the Republican nominee and any qualified independent candidates. Traffic continues on the newer bridge span while the replacement project proceeds.
dek: The former CVS executive defeated Gov. Dan McKee, ending his bid for a second full term amid frustration over the Washington Bridge.
headline: Helena Foulkes defeats Dan McKee in Rhode Island governor primary
